models.name: representativeness_listener
models.rationale: Representativeness listener: reference resolution via diagnostic likelihood ratios. Listeners resolve referring expressions by evaluating how representative or diagnostic each candidate referent is for the spoken description, rather than simulating recursive mental states or applying ungrounded feature penalties. The representativeness of a referent r for an utterance u is determined by the likelihood ratio comparing the probability that a speaker intending r would produce u against the probability that a speaker intending an alternative distractor in the context would produce u. On prior trials where no informative word is spoken, choice is guided by each object's expected representativeness across its features. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

models.name: feature_contrast_listener
models.rationale: Feature contrast listener: non-recursive pragmatic interpretation via unmentioned feature penalty. Rather than inverting a counterfactual speaker, the listener evaluates candidate referents directly according to feature contrast. Matching referents are penalized for each additional unmentioned feature they possess, favouring objects whose features are most exhaustively described. Prior-elicitation trials reflect the object salience prior over feature count and familiarization base rate. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

models.name: distinctiveness_neutral_prior (exported)
models.rationale: Distinctiveness heuristic listener with neutral prior: contextual distinctiveness heuristic without prior bias. Listeners interpret referring expressions using a non-Bayesian perceptual distinctiveness heuristic rather than recursive speaker simulation. When an utterance is heard, listeners restrict attention to matching referents and select the object that is most contextually distinctive in the visual display, possessing features that are rarest across the other objects. On prior trials without an informative description, choice is guided by a neutral object prior that reflects familiarization base rates without an intrinsic distinctiveness bias. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

models.name: feature_contrast_referential_salience (pruned)
models.rationale: Feature contrast listener with referential salience. Refines the incumbent feature_contrast_listener by incorporating referential salience (taken from rsa_l1_referential_salience). Listeners interpret referring expressions through direct feature contrast by penalizing matching referents for additional unmentioned features against a feature-count and familiarization prior. However, on unprompted prior-elicitation trials with no informative word, participants exhibit no baseline preference for feature-rich objects and fall back to uniform guessing. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

models.name: rsa_l1_shared_prior (seed)
models.rationale: RSA pragmatic listener (depth 1) with a salience prior at every level. As the salience model, but the prior over objects is common knowledge: the literal listener the speaker simulates uses it too (the paper's "mutual knowledge" variant), so salience shapes which word a speaker would choose as well as the listener's inference. Salience is a softmax of w_features per feature an object has plus w_familiar times its familiarization base rate. With no informative word the choice is that prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

metric.lede: How well each model predicts which referent people pick in the held-out conditions: conditions of the same papers that the loop never saw. Every model was fitted to the loop's training trials only. The panels show people's choice proportions against the models' predictions for each held-out game, word and condition.
metric.standing_note: Held-out log predictive density behind the best of these models, in nats (whiskers ±2 SE of the difference, clustered by held-out condition). Lower is better. r and RMSE compare predicted and observed choice proportions over held-out display cells.
